claims.text: At stage-2, ProductsController.List declares [FromQuery] int? maxPriceVnd = null and, only when it is not null, reassigns query = query.Where(p => p.PriceVnd <= maxPriceVnd) before OrderBy/Skip/Take/Select/ToListAsync.

EF Core translates the Where into the same SQL statement; the stage-2 api logs 'WHERE p.price_vnd <= @maxPriceVnd' before 'ORDER BY p.id' and 'LIMIT ... OFFSET ...' (placeholder names vary with the values).
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: How queries work; lab stage-2 api log category Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Database.Command

claims.text: A query string value that cannot be converted to the parameter's type (maxPriceVnd=abc for int?) is a model binding error; with [ApiController] the request gets an automatic 400 ValidationProblemDetails before the action runs.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Model binding (type conversion errors); Create web APIs, Automatic HTTP 400 responses

claims.text: Lab stage-2: GET /api/v1/products?maxPriceVnd=abc returns 400 application/problem+json with errors.maxPriceVnd ['The value 'abc' is not valid.'].
Model binding only binds declared parameters; a query parameter the action does not declare (e.g. colour=red) is ignored and the request succeeds as if it were absent.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Model binding (targets are action parameters/bound properties); lab: ?maxPriceVnd=500000&colour=red

claims.text: A request without maxPriceVnd leaves the nullable int? parameter null (its default), so no Where is added and every product is paged.
claims.source_hint: ProductsController.cs stage-2 lines 27, 33; ASP.NET Core docs: Model binding, optional parameters

claims.text: Seeded products costing at most 500000 VND are id 2 (450000), 5 (320000) and 8 (280000); ?maxPriceVnd=500000 returns these three.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang db/seed.sql at tag stage-2; lab curl /api/v1/products?maxPriceVnd=500000

claims.text: Because Where comes before Skip/Take in the chain, OFFSET and LIMIT apply to filtered rows: ?maxPriceVnd=500000&limit=2&offset=1 returns products 5 and 8.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs 7.6 LIMIT and OFFSET (applied after WHERE); lab curl ?maxPriceVnd=500000&limit=2&offset=1

claims.text: A filter narrows the same collection, so it belongs as a query parameter on the collection URL, when the result is still the same resource; one endpoint per filter repeats the paging code and does not combine with other conditions.
claims.source_hint: REST API design convention (collection resource plus query options)

claims.text: Filtering in C# after loading every row makes cost grow with the table, not the result, and breaks offset paging because offset would count rows the user never sees.
claims.source_hint: reasoning from the query flow; backend.l2.offset-pagination

claims.text: Two successive LINQ Where calls on the same IQueryable are combined by EF Core into one SQL WHERE with both conditions joined by AND.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: How queries work / query translation; lab api SQL log
